dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do a lot of people come to you for help?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: There was no shortage even before, but after the war, the number of missing people commissions increased significantly. I'm sure you understand...

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: It's not all bad news, though. Being able to help people find their lost friends and loved ones, and seeing their excitement when they're reunited... It makes me feel happy too.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: As for the others... well, let's not bring that up for now. Some of the loss of contact might just be temporary. Perhaps they'll just turn up back at home someday, completely out of the blue?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Hey there! You looking for someone, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're not a client. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: I just know a ton of people, so over time, people have habitually come to me when they need something or someone found.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: If you need help hiring a wayfinder, feel free to contact me. I'll be around here all day, more or less.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Also, don't worry about fees. I'm just helping out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, but I don't need help just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: No worries. Maybe next time, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean by "wayfinder"...?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Oh, I mean a whole bunch of People of the Springs who love exploring Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: If you think about it carefully, their job scope is similar to that of adventurers, they just call themselves something else.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: As you know, our lands are rife with high-temperature regions, and people of our tribe can explore all sorts of places with the aid of our Koholasaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: As such, many from other tribes and tourists alike will hire wayfinders for convenience, whether as navigators or scouts.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Gah! Can't believe I agreed to switch for the night shifts with that kid. What a mess...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About my reputation with the People of the Springs...

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Ah, a friend, come to help! My thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello. What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: This is the Obsidian Totem Pole. You might have seen ones like it in other tribes, but this one belongs to us, the People of the Springs.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: After you complete tribal commissions, the Pole will grant you corresponding recompense — and you'll also have my thanks on behalf of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: As for anything else, go find Caramuru during the day shift! Can't be letting our primary appointment holder get off scot-free, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can't swap back?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: Well, that wouldn't change much, in truth. It's either the day shift or the night one, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: And this is an important spot, so someone's got to watch it.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: I still wanna give Caramuru a smack over the head, of course, but I'm the responsible one between us!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry to bother you.

dialogues.speaker: Kahuna
dialogues.text: It's alright. This is personal business, so don't mind me.
